title: Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) marang: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) marang is a marang variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) is a registered marang variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Mr 01. University of Southern Mindanao bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) marang is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [marang variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) marang
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) was about 8 years old and about 10 meters tall when it was registered. It bears every year, with fruit in July Sept. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

A fruit of Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) weighs about 1614 grams, and its shape is round to oblong. The flesh is white and smooth and fine. Its sweetness measured 25 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 38.4 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as July Sept, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50) marang

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Maraginto (USMARC Accession #50)?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
